readings: z is registered (Moore): the output bit corresponding to x_i appears one clock cycle after x_i is sampled; an initial/reset output 0 is present before the first valid bit.
z is combinational (Mealy-like): the output bit corresponding to x_i appears in the same clock cycle as x_i, requiring z to depend on the current input x as well as the state.
areset is asynchronous and level-sensitive: asserting areset immediately forces state (and possibly z) to the reset value, regardless of clk.
areset is sampled on the positive edge of clk (synchronous): state/z change only at a clk rising edge while areset is asserted, so reset takes effect on the next clock edge.
During areset assertion, z is forced to 0 (initial state output or reset value of an output register).
During areset assertion, z holds its previous value (conversion stopped/hold), and only the internal state is reset.
areset is active high: reset is asserted when areset=1, and conversion begins when areset goes to 0.
areset is active low: reset is asserted when areset=0, and conversion begins when areset goes to 1.
